narrative.overview: Large, heavy type introduces the developer, while full project interfaces supply the evidence. Flat light-gray fields and oxblood text give the page a clear identity without surrounding the work with decorative controls. Project explanations remain substantial and readable.
keyCharacteristics: One self-hosted sans-serif family with a strong display weight.
Large type, rectangular controls, and full-width tonal sections.
Real project screenshots with explicit preview captions where needed.
Readable content and native interactions that remain useful without JavaScript.

rules.name: The Tonal Field Rule
rules.body: Separate major regions through flat background changes and spacing; the implemented system uses no gradients, shadows, or outlined cards.

dos: Do keep substantive explanations at the readable body size and use muted text for secondary information.
Do retain flat section fields, a consistent wrapper, and square controls.
Do use actual project imagery with explicit provenance and preview captions.
Do preserve keyboard focus, native link/disclosure behavior, reduced motion, and a complete no-JavaScript reading experience.
Do update factual status, screenshots, and links together when the projects change.
donts: Don't replace evidence with invented project outcomes, fictional interfaces, or unsupported completion claims.
Don't add shadows, gradients, rounded card containers, or a second typeface to this established visual system without a deliberate redesign.
Don't hide required content until an animation or script finishes.
Don't present the SheetShift browser preview as a functioning web converter.
